questions.question: The accounting equation states that:
options: ASSETS equal OWNER'S EQUITY plus LIABILITIES — what the business owns is financed by the owner and by outsiders, at every moment

questions.question: Double entry exists because:
options: Two bookkeepers must check each other
The equation must stay level — so every transaction has two equal effects, a debit and a credit

questions.question: On the debit-credit compass:
options: Assets, expenses and drawings increase DEBIT; equity, liabilities and income increase CREDIT

questions.question: The owner deposits R15 000 capital. The double effect is:
options: Debit Bank R15 000 (asset up), credit Capital R15 000 (equity up) — and the equation stays level

questions.question: A credit note issued to a debtor is the source document for:
options: The Debtors Allowances Journal — goods a debtor sends back

questions.question: Cash sales of R7 500 with cost of sales R6 000 are recorded:
options: Both in the CRJ — the perpetual system records the sale AND the shelf's loss together (mark-up check: 6 000 × 1,25 = 7 500)
Sales in the CRJ, cost of sales in the CPJ

questions.question: Stock bought on credit from the wholesaler for R4 000 goes to:
options: The Creditors Journal, from the original invoice

questions.question: The two facts that choose the door for every transaction are:
options: The account name and the balance
Cash or credit, and which direction the value moves

subtopics.title: Posting, Balancing and the Trial Balance That Proves It

questions.question: The bank account's closing balance is:
Debtors control closes at:
options: R800 debit — 2 500 owed, less the 500 allowance, less the 1 200 payment

questions.question: The trial balance totals are:
options: R26 000 both sides — debits: bank, stock, debtors, cost of sales, rent, wages; credits: capital, sales, creditors

questions.question: A level trial balance CANNOT detect:
options: A casting error in one account only
An amount posted to the WRONG account, or a transaction left out on both sides

questions.question: The control account and the individual accounts differ in that:
options: The control is built from JOURNAL TOTALS; the individual pages from INDIVIDUAL POSTINGS — the same street counted twice by different routes

questions.question: The debtors agreement for the month shows:
options: Control R800 (sales 2 500 less allowances 500 less receipts 1 200) equal to Mr Naidoo's page: 2 500 − 500 − 1 200 = R800
No agreement is possible with one debtor

questions.question: A receipt written onto the wrong customer's page:
options: Disturbs the control but not the list
Disturbs the list but not the control — the journal totals were still right

questions.question: The creditors side of the check shows:
options: No control account exists for creditors
Control R1 500 (purchases 4 000 less payments 2 500) matching the wholesaler's page at R1 500

questions.question: The two questions that sort every slip are:
options: Did cash move, or a promise? And which way did the value travel?
How much, and who signed it?
Is it big enough to record?

questions.question: The wholesaler's invoice of R4 000 belongs in:
options: The receipts box — cash came in
The invoice-in box — a promise, value coming in from the supplier

questions.question: After the sorting, each tidy pile becomes:
options: A page in the exercise book
One journal, already totalled, ready for the ledger

subtopics.title: The Month That Adds Up Twice

questions.question: The ledger answers a question the shoebox cannot, namely:
options: "Where do we STAND?" — regrouping the month by thing: bank R11 500, stock R2 900, Mr Naidoo R800

questions.question: The weigh-in works because:
options: The shop weighs its cash box
Every entry all month was an equal pair — so debit balances and credit balances must weigh the same: R26 000 each side

questions.question: The level scale's blind spot is that it cannot smell:
options: A debit larger than its credit
A pair written onto the wrong pages, or a slip that never reached the shoebox at all

questions.question: The two records of the same street are:
options: The exercise book with a page per customer, and the main books' single total line — built from different papers
The bank statement and the till tape
Two copies of the same journal
The budget and the actual figures

questions.question: In Lerato's month, the two counts agree at:
options: R800 each — the sum of the customer pages beside the total line

questions.question: A payment written on the wrong customer's page means:
options: The total line is wrong, the pages right
The exercise book is wrong, the total line right — the difference itself gives directions

questions.question: The year's whole machine, in five habits, is:
options: Sort the slips, write the diaries, gather the ledger, weigh the trial balance, count the street twice
